The program is aimed at strengthening management of community forests and protected areas in Liberia through improved governance of community forest management bodies, capacity building of forest regulatory institutions, and promotion of sustainable livelihood incentives for forest dependent communities.

The project seeks to strengthen management of community forests and protected areas in Liberia through improved capacity of community forest management bodies, capacity building of forest regulatory institutions, empowerment of forest and farm producer organizations, and promotion of sustainable livelihood incentives for forest fringe communities.
The following are the results that are envisaged at the end of the project:
1. Strengthened institutional and community capacity, and regulatory framework for community forest management
2. Status of key species and their habitat improved due to participatory forest management and biodiversity conservation
3. Livelihood options for communities are made climate-resilient through diversification, enterprise development
4. Knowledge management system built /strengthened to support gender-balanced community forest management and co-management of protected areas.

description.narrative:
Below are some key results of the project as of April 2026. It is important to also keep in mind that year 4 report which is due end of May/early June 2026 is expected to narrate more up to date results.
Summary of key results achieved up to date
Strengthened Community Forest Governance
1. Community governance structures are being fully established and operationalized in three Authorized Forest Communities (AFCs), improving accountability and participatory forest management.
2. Seven applicant forest communities (covering 70,024 ha) advanced to higher authorization stages (steps 58), reflecting stronger compliance with legal and governance requirements.
3. Community Forest Management Plans (CFMPs) for 71,995 ha were reviewed and strengthened, contributing to more sustainable forest management practices.
Expanded Capacity Building and Local Ownership
1,169 individuals (42% women) enhanced their skills in advocacy, leadership, gender mainstreaming, Community Rights Law, land rights, biodiversity conservation, and participatory mapping. These efforts are contributing to strengthened community leadership, increased transparency, and deepened local ownership of forest governance processes.
Improved Livelihoods and Economic Resilience
1. More than 1,500 direct beneficiaries (65% women) were supported with incomeearning ventures through diversified livelihood activities such as lowland rice farming, animal husbandry, beekeeping, cassava processing, vegetable production, arts and crafts, and participation in VSLAs.
2. 149,000 cocoa seedlings were distributed to 250 farmers (40% women), laying the foundation for new cocoa farms expected to generate income within the coming years.
